author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Brown field hockey rallied from two goals down in the fourth quarter and defeated Boston University 5-4 after a shootout Friday at Goldberger Family Field. The Bears trailed 4-2 with 13:40 remaining before Sophia Clark and Kate Siedem scored 59 seconds apart to force overtime.

Neither team scored in the extra period, sending the match to a shootout. Kiersten Smith, Julia Lattuada and Mia Karine Myklebust converted for Brown, with Myklebust producing the deciding goal in a 3-2 shootout advantage. Goalkeeper Ellie Parker matched a career high with 10 saves after Boston University controlled long stretches of possession.

Grace Almeida, Smith, Siedem and Clark accounted for Brown’s four regulation goals. The Terriers had opened a 2-0 lead in the second quarter, and later moved ahead 4-2 early in the fourth before the comeback. Brown improved to 2-1 and earned its second straight victory. The Bears are next scheduled to travel to Fairfield for another nonconference match.
dek: The Bears tied the game in the fourth quarter and won a shootout 3-2, with Mia Karine Myklebust supplying the deciding attempt.
headline: Brown field hockey erases two-goal deficit to beat Boston University
